data.name: Gal-X-E
data.detailed_description:
//[{Brief Overview}]\

Gal-X-E aims to revive the old-school shoot em up genre, and adds modern elements to it! Fight your way through endless waves of randomly generated madness! Collect spaceships and show the enemy who's boss!

//[{GamePlay}]\

Gal-X-E offers unique and interesting gameplay. Unlike traditional modern games where players can upgrade themselves until their power level reaches "Over 9000!", Gal-X-E relies on the actual skill of the player. Even though Gal-X-E offers new spaceships to be built, they only provide minimal improvement. All classes are completely unique in the way that they play, so try to find the one that suits you the most! Players are thrown into an arena where they fight of hordes of never-ending enemies. Kill enemies and collect score multipliers to gain incredible amounts of points!

//[{Spaceships}]\

Gal-X-E presents the player with 24 different spaceships, divided into 6 unique classes as follows:

Light: High agility, as well as a rapid fire-rate with low accuracy.

Medium: Normal firing rate, higher damage, and slower speeds.

Heavy: Low fire rate, high damage, and good accuracy. It's almost a portable cannon.

Shotgun: Capable of dealing devastating damage, though you'll have to get uncomfortably close to maximize the effect.

Sniper: These bad boys are 100% accurate, and deal one shot one kill hits. You'll have no excuse for missing this time!

Chaingun: The most inaccurate, yet highest damage class! It's basically spray and pray for noobs.

//[{Enemies}]\

Every enemy in Gal-X-E provides an unique challenge to overcome, but we won't go about spoiling your fun by telling you what to expect.

//{[Languages]}\

Currently only English is supported, but the interface is self explanatory so that anyone from any language can enjoy it!

//{[Features]}\

The main game consists of randomly generated waves of enemies, meaning that not one play through will be the same! The longer you survive, the more intense the waves become!

The Hangar is where you can open loot boxes in the hopes of finding a brand new, shiny spaceship!

The Badges screen is where you can view your current badges and your progress on those you still need to earn. Badges are basically achievements but with CRAZY challenges!

The Stats screen allow you to be disappointed in your life when you see how much of your life you've wasted on this game.

//{[Conclusion]}\

If you're into old-school arcade fun, as well as games that rely mainly on the improving of the player's skill, Gal-X-E is for you!

reviews.review:
Gal-X-E is a straightforward arcade shoot ’em up that builds its identity around survival, escalating enemy pressure, and the pursuit of increasingly impressive scores. Developed and published by Volens Nolens Games, it avoids unnecessary complexity and instead concentrates on the fundamentals of movement, shooting, positioning, and staying alive as long as possible. Its design clearly favors players who enjoy replayable arcade challenges rather than story-heavy campaigns, making every attempt primarily about improving personal performance and becoming more comfortable with the available spacecraft.

The main gameplay revolves around surviving randomly generated waves of enemies that become increasingly difficult over time. Early encounters provide enough breathing room to become accustomed to movement and weapon behavior, but surviving longer steadily introduces greater pressure. The unpredictable wave structure means that players cannot simply memorize an exact sequence and repeat it indefinitely. Instead, they must react to changing enemy combinations, identify immediate threats, and constantly reposition themselves. This helps maintain some variety even though the underlying objective remains largely unchanged throughout each session.

Scoring plays an important role in making the survival format more engaging. Eliminating enemies and maintaining effective combat performance can contribute toward larger scores and multipliers, encouraging players to do more than simply avoid danger. Aggressive play can be rewarding, but it also creates additional opportunities for mistakes. This produces a satisfying risk-versus-reward relationship where pursuing a better score can mean placing the ship in situations that would otherwise be unnecessary. Players interested in leaderboards, personal records, and mechanical improvement will find this approach considerably more appealing than those looking for a traditional beginning-to-end campaign.

Ship variety provides much of the game's long-term experimentation. There are 24 spacecraft distributed across six classes, with each category emphasizing a different combat philosophy. Light ships prioritize speed and rapid attacks at the expense of accuracy, while Medium ships offer a more balanced combination of mobility and offensive ability. Heavy ships sacrifice speed and firing frequency in exchange for powerful, accurate attacks. These fundamental differences ensure that changing ships is more meaningful than simply selecting a different visual design.

The remaining classes move further toward specialized play styles. Shotgun ships reward players willing to engage enemies at relatively close distances, where their concentrated offensive capabilities become most effective. Sniper ships favor deliberate accuracy and highly damaging precision attacks. Chaingun ships emphasize tremendous sustained firepower while accepting weaker accuracy as the tradeoff. Having these distinct categories gives players opportunities to discover a preferred approach while also encouraging experimentation when a familiar strategy becomes repetitive.

An important design choice is that unlocking additional spacecraft does not necessarily mean obtaining something objectively superior. Progression is more horizontal than purely power-based, with different ships providing alternative characteristics instead of automatically making earlier choices obsolete. This keeps skill at the center of the experience. A player who has spent more time unlocking content still needs to understand positioning, firing patterns, enemy behavior, and survival fundamentals. It is a sensible system for an arcade game because success continues to feel connected to personal improvement rather than accumulated upgrades.

Outside individual survival attempts, the Hangar provides a collection component where loot boxes can produce additional ships. This gives players another incentive to keep playing beyond chasing scores. Badges provide particularly difficult challenges for those interested in completing demanding objectives, while statistics allow players to examine their overall performance. These secondary systems do not radically transform the game, but they provide useful milestones and make repeated sessions feel slightly more purposeful.

The presentation remains appropriately modest and functional. Gal-X-E does not attempt to disguise itself as a cinematic space adventure or narrative-driven science-fiction experience. Its emphasis is immediate action, recognizable threats, and a gameplay loop that can be understood without extensive preparation. That accessibility makes it suitable for shorter sessions. Starting another attempt after being overwhelmed requires little commitment, which can create the familiar arcade feeling of repeatedly trying for just one better run.

Repetition is nevertheless the game's biggest weakness. Randomly generated waves create variation, but the core activity remains endless survival against increasingly difficult enemies. Players who require frequent environmental changes, extensive narrative development, elaborate character progression, or a large handcrafted campaign may find the experience limited. The collection system and badges extend its lifespan, but their effectiveness depends heavily on whether the player already enjoys repeating the central combat loop.

Steam Deck compatibility is not officially established through a Steam Deck Verified or Playable designation. The game should therefore be treated as having an unknown or unsupported official Deck status rather than being presented as fully certified for Valve's handheld. Its relatively lightweight arcade design may make it possible to run through SteamOS and Proton, but successful operation should not be assumed to equal official compatibility. Players primarily intending to use a Steam Deck should be prepared for possible control, display, launcher, or compatibility adjustments.

Overall, Gal-X-E works best as a focused arcade diversion built for players who value mechanical improvement and score chasing. The randomized waves provide uncertainty, the six ship classes introduce genuine differences in play style, and the 24 spacecraft create a respectable amount of experimentation within a deliberately compact framework. Its repetitive nature prevents it from having the broader appeal of a more elaborate shoot ’em up, but the emphasis on skill rather than overwhelming upgrades gives the experience a solid foundation. For players who enjoy short, increasingly difficult survival runs and gradually mastering different combat styles, it offers a simple but reasonably rewarding challenge.

Rating: 7/10
